name: Daily Use
summary: Covers the retained user's typical daily interaction with Taskly — opening the app, reviewing tasks, and marking items complete. Users in this phase are broadly satisfied but the lack of proactive reminders means the app depends entirely on the user to remember to open it, limiting its effectiveness as a productivity tool.

stages.name: Open App
actions: Remembers they need to check their tasks
Finds and opens the Taskly app
Reviews the task list for the day
thoughts: I keep forgetting to check this
I should add this to my morning routine
I wish this reminded me to open it

emotions.label: Satisfied
emotions.description: Generally positive about the tool when they remember to use it, but the reliance on manual habit formation is a fragile engagement model

painPoints: No reminders or notifications to prompt users to open the app and check their tasks
App has no home screen widget, so it competes with dozens of other app icons for attention
opportunities: Push notifications for due tasks to bring users back to the app at the right moment
Build a home screen widget showing today's task count and the next due item

stages.name: Check Tasks
touchpoints: Taskly app — home screen task list
actions: Identifies which tasks are due today
Re-prioritises or reschedules tasks as needed
thoughts: Which of these actually needs doing today?
I have too many things listed — I need to trim this down
I forgot I had added that

emotions.label: Satisfied
emotions.description: The task list is genuinely useful for recalling outstanding work, though an overloaded list can shift the mood toward mild anxiety

painPoints: No smart or AI-assisted prioritisation — users manually decide what to tackle each day
Overdue tasks accumulate without a clear prompt to reschedule or dismiss them
opportunities: Daily digest view that automatically surfaces the three most important tasks for today
Overdue task prompt — a weekly nudge to reschedule or archive stale items

stages.name: Mark Complete
touchpoints: Taskly app — home screen task list
actions: Works through tasks during the day
Returns to Taskly to tick off completed items
Feels a sense of accomplishment at end of day
thoughts: That satisfying tick is the best part
I wish I could see a summary of what I got done this week
I should add tomorrow's tasks before I close the app

emotions.label: Satisfied
emotions.description: Completion interactions are the emotional high point of the daily journey — users report genuine satisfaction from ticking off tasks

painPoints: No weekly or daily completion summary to reinforce progress and the habit loop
No reminders or notifications for tasks approaching their due time during the day
opportunities: End-of-day summary notification showing tasks completed and tasks still open
Due-time push notifications for tasks with a specific time set, surfaced at the right moment

insights.text: Users who enable at least one notification retain at 2x the rate of users with all notifications off at the 30-day mark
In exit surveys, 'no reminders' was cited as a reason for churning by 41% of users who cancelled in their first month
5 of 7 interview participants said they would use the app more if it sent them a morning reminder listing their tasks for the day
